claim.why_it_matters: Its sibling 2.2.5 Communication Status Key Conditions (page 672) and 2.2.4 General Rules are '###' headings under '## 2.2 THE COMMUNICATION DESCRIPTION ENTRY'; at '##' the 2.2.6 heading becomes a peer of 2.2 instead of its child, breaking the heading outline.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page XIV-16 shows the heading '2.2.6 Error Key Values', a third-level paragraph number under 2.2. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md the parent '## 2.2 THE COMMUNICATION DESCRIPTION ENTRY' is at '##' and its siblings '### 2.2.4 General Rules' and '### 2.2.5 Communication Status Key Conditions' are at '###', but this heading is written '## 2.2.6 Error Key Values'. That makes 2.2.6 a peer of 2.2 in the outline. The heading text is correct; only its level is wrong. This is a structural defect with no normative effect.
verdict.corrected_description: The heading text is present and correct, but its level is wrong: '## 2.2.6' should be '### 2.2.6' to match its siblings 2.2.4 and 2.2.5 under '## 2.2'. (The claim's kind 'missing-heading' really means a wrong heading level.)
